title: Calibration curation policy for long-tail intent representation
creator: Aisha Martinez
description: Design and implement a repeatable policy for constructing per-domain calibration packs that explicitly surface long-tail intents and rare prompt shapes for FP8 and INT8 quantization validation. The work covers sampling rules, pack size targets, balancing between frequent/rare intents, context-length bucketing, negative/contrast example inclusion, and tooling to synthesize lightweight augmentations where data is insufficient. The goal is to reduce accuracy regressions introduced by quantized kernels on low-frequency behaviors observed in production traffic.
objectives: Define sampling strata and priority weights to surface long-tail intents without inflating pack size
Establish per-domain target pack compositions (intent coverage, context-length buckets, tenant-weight floor)
Ship a curation pipeline that outputs manifest JSON + example RNG seeds for reproducible calibration packs
Integrate pack generation with the quant calibration runner and validation harness to produce per-model accuracy deltas
Document evaluation guidelines and acceptance thresholds for FP8/INT8 rollouts
acceptance_criteria: For >=90% of domains, calibration pack contains at least 12 distinct long-tail intent examples (frequency < 0.1% of domain traffic)
Pack composition includes context-length buckets: short (<64 tokens), medium (64-256), long (256-1024) with at least 10% examples in long bucket for dialogue-heavy domains
Automated pack builder produces reproducible manifest and summary metrics (coverage, avg token length, token distribution) and stores them in Drive/Confluence

Validation harness reports per-domain model delta metrics: KL divergence on token distributions < 0.006 and end-to-end task accuracy drop <= 1.5% for INT8 / <=2.5% for FP8 (or documented model-specific thresholds)
Playbook entry created in Confluence describing when to regenerate packs and how to interpret failure modes
design-decisions: Use hybrid sampling: reservoir sampling for frequent intents + importance-weighted oversampling for rare intents using a capped boost factor to avoid dominating the pack
Apply context-length stratification first, then perform intent-level balancing within each bucket to preserve the joint distribution of length and intent
Include contrastive negatives: for each long-tail positive example, include 1-2 near-miss prompts sampled from the same cohort to surface small-output divergences after quantization
Synthesize paraphrases only for intents with <5 examples using a lightweight templated augmentation pipeline; mark synthetic examples in the manifest
Enforce tenant privacy by hashing tenant ids and imposing per-tenant floor of 1 example per pack where applicable; exclude PII via existing redaction pipeline
implementation-plan: Week 1: Draft sampling spec and simulated results using last 90-day production logs (privacy-safe aggregates)
Week 2: Implement pack builder + reproducible manifest generator; add context-length bucketing and rarity scoring
Week 3: Hook builder into quant calibration runner; run baseline INT8/FP8 calibration on two representative models and compare metrics
Week 4: Iterate thresholds based on observed failure modes; author Confluence playbook and add auto-regeneration cron job for high-change domains
outstanding-risks: Overfitting to sampled calibration packs — packs may not reflect sudden emergent intents; mitigation: short regeneration window and traffic-aware recency boost
Synthetic paraphrases could create unrealistic distributions — mitigation: label synthetic data and exclude from metric baselines used for rollout decisions
Per-tenant skew where a single tenant dominates rare-intent examples — mitigation: enforce per-tenant caps and minimum representation
Validation thresholds may require model-specific tuning — mitigation: include a calibration-to-production mapping step in the playbook
